बॉलीवु़ड के गलियारों से आ रही है एकदम मसालेदार खबर! 🔥
निटेश तिवारी की फिल्म Ramayana 5 नवंबर को रिलीज होने के बाद से ही बॉक्स ऑफिस पर धूम मचा रही है।
फिल्म में सीता के योद्धा रूप को लेकर दर्शकों के एक वर्ग ने सवाल उठाए और कड़ी आलोचना की है।
लेकिन अब फिल्म में कैकेयी का रोल निभाने वाली Lara Dutta ने इस पर खुलकर बात की है और आलोचकों से छोटी सोच छोड़ने को कहा है।
Lara Dutta ने NDTV को दिए इंटरव्यू में कहा कि दर्शकों को सिर्फ cinematic experience का मजा लेना चाहिए।
उनका कहना है कि राजपरिवार के बच्चों को हथियारों की ट्रेनिंग मिलती थी और सीता जैसी महिला 14 साल के वनवास के दौरान खुद की रक्षा करती ही।
मेकर्स का यह भी दावा है कि सीता के इस रूप की प्रेरणा Adbhuta Ramayana से ली गई है, जिसमें वह भयंकर रूप में नजर आती हैं।
दूसरी तरफ, दर्शकों ने ज्यादातर Valmiki Ramayana और Ramanand Sagar की television series Ramayan देखी है, जिससे यह बहस छिड़ी है।
Nitesh Tiwari के निर्देशन में बनी इस फिल्म में Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash और Ravi Dubey जैसे बड़े कलाकार हैं।
फिल्म ने पहले हफ्ते में ही worldwide 1,000 करोड़ रुपये का आंकड़ा पार कर लिया है और यह ₹ 4,000 crore के बजट में बनी है।
क्या आपके हिसाब से माइथोलॉजिकल फिल्मों में क्रिएटिव लिबर्टी लेना सही है या गलत? नीचे कमेंट्स में बताओ! 👇✨

ctx.title: Lara Dutta defends Sai Pallavi's warrior Sita in Ramayana amid backlash, asks critics to stop being ‘small-minded’
ctx.summary: Lara Dutta has defended Sai Pallavi’s portrayal of Sita as a warrior in Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana, saying royal children may have trained in combat at that time.
ctx.text:
Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana has been making waves at the box office ever since its release on November 5. However, Sita's portrayal as a warrior who fights demons in the film has raised eyebrows and drawn criticism from a section of viewers. Now, Lara Dutta , who essays the role of Kaikeyi in the film, has defended the portrayal and urged people not to be small-minded.
In an interview with NDTV, Lara defended Sai Pallavi's portrayal of Sita as a warrior amid the backlash, insisting that audiences should simply enjoy the cinematic experience. She pointed out that there are several versions of the Ramayana. She also noted that, considering the cultural practices of those times, boys and girls born into royal families were trained in both the arts and the use of weapons.
She added, “So when you look at things like that, there are so many possibilities of what could have happened, should have happened, whatever. So I think it's not that far off or it's not that far-fetched to think that Sita was also possibly very much trained in the art of warfare. And especially, I mean, I just say that when you're put into a situation like that also as a woman, you're not going to be a helpless woman.”
Lara further said that a character like Sita, who chooses to spend 14 years in exile in the forest, would also have to be resilient. “At some point, she will pick up something to defend herself. You have to stop being so small-minded, you know, and also embrace the cinematic experience,” she said.
Ramayana shows Sita wielding a sword and fighting demons alongside Lord Rama. She is also shown training children and local youths in combat. The portrayal of Sita as a warrior in Nitesh Tiwari's film sparked a debate among viewers, with some questioning the creative liberties taken with a character deeply rooted in religious beliefs and mythology. However, the makers had earlier revealed that they had drawn inspiration for Sita's portrayal as a warrior from the Adbhuta Ramayana.
The Adbhuta Ramayana depicts Sita's fierce and divine aspect, in which she assumes a powerful form, often associated with Goddess Kali, to defeat Sahasra Ravana, a thousand-headed demon. On the other hand, Indian audiences have largely grown up watching adaptations of Valmiki's Ramayana, including Ramanand Sagar's television series Ramayan.
Helmed by Nitesh Tiwari and backed by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The film has crossed the ₹ 1,000-crore mark worldwide within its first week. Made on a massive budget of ₹ 4,000 crore, the film is scheduled to release in two parts, with the second instalment set to arrive in 2028.
